title: Novena to St. Rita
description: A nine-day prayer for impossible causes and difficult marriages. St. Rita is known as the 'Saint of the Impossible' and is the patron saint of impossible causes, difficult marriages, and abused women.
intention: For impossible causes, difficult marriages, and desperate situations
instructions: Pray this novena for 9 consecutive days with faith and trust in God's power to do the impossible. St. Rita is known for miracles both during her life and after her death. She is often invoked when situations seem hopeless or when all human efforts have failed. Include your personal intentions during each day of prayer, particularly those that seem impossible.
background_info: St. Rita was born in 1381 in Roccaporena, Italy. Despite her desire to become a nun, she was married at age 12 to Paolo Mancini, a cruel and violent man. Through her patience, prayers, and kindness, she eventually converted him, but he was murdered by his enemies. She prevented her sons from seeking revenge, and they both died shortly after. Rita then sought to enter the Augustinian convent but was initially refused. Through her prayers, a famous family feud was reconciled, and she was admitted. She lived as an Augustinian nun for 40 years, known for her deep prayer life, austerity, and charity. Near the end of her life, she received a partial stigmata - a wound from a thorn of Christ's crown appeared on her forehead. She is called the 'Saint of the Impossible' because she achieved what seemed impossible: converting her violent husband, reconciling feuding families, and entering the convent despite seemingly insurmountable obstacles.

days.title: Day 1: Trusting God with the Impossible
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Rita, saint of the impossible, you who experienced so many situations that seemed hopeless, teach me to trust in God's power to do what seems impossible. When I face troubles that have no human solution, help me to turn to God with complete confidence. You knew that nothing is impossible for God, and your life testifies to His power to transform the most difficult circumstances. Intercede for me, that I may have your unwavering faith. Pray that God will help me in my need: [mention your request]. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Rita, advocate of impossible cases, pray for us.
days.reflection: St. Rita's entire life was a testimony to God's ability to do the impossible. Her marriage seemed beyond hope, her sons seemed destined for murder, her vocation seemed blocked. Yet God worked through all these impossibilities. Today, bring your impossible situation to God with the same trust.
days.intention_prayer: St. Rita, I bring my impossible situation to you: [pour out your heart]. Help me to believe that nothing is impossible for God.
days.scripture: "For nothing is impossible with God." - Luke 1:37

days.title: Day 2: Suffering with Dignity
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Rita, you endured abuse and cruelty in your marriage with patience and dignity. You did not allow bitterness to poison your soul, but responded to evil with good. Help me when I suffer unjustly. Teach me to maintain my dignity and my faith even when others treat me cruelly. Give me the strength to forgive those who hurt me and to pray for those who persecute me. Let my suffering, united to Christ's, become a source of grace. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Rita, advocate of impossible cases, pray for us.
days.reflection: St. Rita's husband was violent and unfaithful for many years. Rather than becoming bitter or giving up, she prayed for him and responded to his cruelty with kindness. Her patience eventually won his conversion. Suffering does not have to break us – it can make us holy when we unite it to Christ's suffering.
days.intention_prayer: St. Rita, I pray for those who suffer abuse or injustice: [name yourself or others]. Help them to maintain their dignity and to trust in God's justice.
days.scripture: "But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you." - Matthew 5:44

days.title: Day 3: Forgiving Enemies
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Rita, when your husband was murdered, you forgave his killers and prevented your sons from seeking revenge. You understood that hatred only breeds more hatred, and that forgiveness breaks the cycle of violence. Help me to forgive those who have hurt me and my loved ones. Free me from the prison of resentment and the desire for revenge. Give me the grace to pray for my enemies, that I may be truly free and that God's peace may reign in my heart. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Rita, advocate of impossible cases, pray for us.
days.reflection: In Rita's time and place, avenging a family member's murder was expected. Yet Rita had already learned to forgive. She pleaded with her sons not to seek revenge, and when they died before they could carry out their plans, she saw it as God's mercy preventing bloodshed. True freedom comes through forgiveness.
days.intention_prayer: St. Rita, I pray for the grace to forgive: [name those who have hurt you]. Help me to let go of resentment and to pray for those who have wronged me.
days.scripture: "Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, 'Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother or sister who sins against me? Up to seven times?' Jesus answered, 'I tell you, not seven times, but seventy-seven times.'" - Matthew 18:21-22

days.title: Day 4: Persistence in Prayer
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Rita, you prayed for years for your husband's conversion and for your sons' souls. You prayed for entrance to the convent when it seemed blocked. You never stopped praying, even when answers seemed far away. Teach me to persist in prayer. When I am tempted to give up, remind me that God hears every prayer and will answer in His perfect time. Help me to pray with faith, patience, and perseverance. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Rita, advocate of impossible cases, pray for us.
days.reflection: St. Rita prayed for about eighteen years for her husband's conversion. She prayed for peace between feuding families. She prayed to enter the convent. She understood that persistent prayer is not nagging God but cooperating with His timing. Each prayer is a seed that will bear fruit in due season.
days.intention_prayer: St. Rita, help me to persist in prayer for: [name your long-standing requests]. Give me grace to wait with faith and hope.
days.scripture: "And will not God bring about justice for his chosen ones, who cry out to him day and night? Will he keep putting them off? I tell you, he will see that they get justice, and quickly." - Luke 18:7-8

days.title: Day 5: Accepting God's Will
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Rita, you desired to become a nun from your youth, but accepted marriage when your parents arranged it. When you later sought to enter the convent, you accepted the initial rejection. Through all of life's changes, you sought to do God's will, not your own. Help me to discern and accept God's will in my life, even when it differs from my plans. Give me the grace to say with Mary, 'Be it done to me according to your word.' Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Rita, advocate of impossible cases, pray for us.
days.reflection: St. Rita's life took turns she did not expect or desire. She wanted to be a nun but was forced into marriage. She came to love her husband only to lose him. She wanted to enter the convent but was rejected. Through it all, she accepted God's will with humility and trust. Surrendering to God's will brings peace even in confusing circumstances.
days.intention_prayer: St. Rita, help me to accept God's will in my life: [express your struggles with God's plan]. Give me the grace to trust that His plans are good.
days.scripture: "For I know the plans I have for you, declares the Lord, plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you hope and a future." - Jeremiah 29:11

days.title: Day 6: Peace in Family Conflict
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Rita, peacemaker and reconciler, you brought peace between feuding families when it seemed impossible. Your prayers ended violence and restored harmony. Help me to be an instrument of peace in my family and community. Where there is conflict, bring reconciliation. Where there is resentment, bring forgiveness. Where there is division, bring unity. Use me to heal broken relationships and to build peace. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Rita, advocate of impossible cases, pray for us.
days.reflection: The feuds between families in Cascia were violent and long-standing. Many had died in the cycle of revenge. Yet Rita's prayers and witness brought about peace between the families, which opened the door for her to enter the convent. Peace is possible even in the most divided families when we bring them to God in prayer.
days.intention_prayer: St. Rita, I pray for peace in these troubled relationships: [name family conflicts]. Help me to be an instrument of your peace.
days.scripture: "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God." - Matthew 5:9

days.title: Day 7: The Thorn of Suffering
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Rita, you received a thorn from Christ's crown, a visible sign of your union with His suffering. For fifteen years you bore this painful wound, offering it for the salvation of souls. Help me to accept my own sufferings with grace. Teach me to unite my pain to Christ's sacrifice, that it may become redemptive. When I suffer, let me remember that Christ suffered first, and that sharing His suffering means sharing His glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Rita, advocate of impossible cases, pray for us.
days.reflection: When St. Rita asked to share in Christ's suffering, she received a thorn wound on her forehead that remained until her death. She saw this as a privilege, not a burden – a sign of her deep union with Jesus. Our suffering, united to Christ's, has meaning and can bring grace to others.
days.intention_prayer: St. Rita, I offer my sufferings to God: [name your sufferings]. Unite them to Christ's suffering for the salvation of souls.
days.scripture: "I want to know Christ—yes, to know the power of his resurrection and participation in his sufferings, becoming like him in his death." - Philippians 3:10

days.title: Day 8: The Desire for Holiness
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Rita, you lived forty years as a religious nun, growing in holiness through prayer, penance, and charity. Your life in the convent was marked by deep devotion to the Passion of Christ and loving service to others. Help me to grow in holiness in my own state of life. Whether in marriage or consecrated life, in work or in rest, make me holy as You are holy. Let my life be a witness to Your love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Rita, advocate of impossible cases, pray for us.
days.reflection: St. Rita's holiness was not just for the dramatic moments; it was cultivated through daily prayer, sacrifice, and service. She meditated deeply on Christ's Passion, served the poor, and lived simply. Holiness is not about extraordinary moments but about faithfulness in ordinary life.
days.intention_prayer: St. Rita, help me to grow in holiness. Show me how to be faithful to God in my daily life: [express your desire for holiness].
days.scripture: "But just as he who called you is holy, so be holy in all you do; for it is written: 'Be holy, because I am holy.'" - 1 Peter 1:15-16

days.title: Day 9: Thanksgiving for Miracles
days.opening_prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
days.daily_prayer: Dear St. Rita, your life was marked by miracles – from the conversion of your husband to the reconciliation of feuding families, from your acceptance into the convent to your union with Christ's suffering. Since your death, countless miracles have been granted through your intercession. As this novena concludes, I thank God for the miracles He has already worked in my life and for those He will yet perform. Help me to trust that God hears my prayers and will answer according to His perfect will. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
days.closing_prayer: St. Rita, advocate of impossible cases, pray for us.
days.reflection: St. Rita is called upon daily by thousands seeking the impossible. Her shrine in Cascia draws pilgrims from around the world. Many miracles have been attributed to her intercession. As we conclude this novena, we trust that God is at work – even if we cannot yet see the answer. St. Rita reminds us that nothing is impossible with God.
days.intention_prayer: St. Rita, I thank God for hearing my prayers. I entrust my impossible requests to your intercession: [state your requests]. I trust that God will answer in His perfect way and time.
days.scripture: "Jesus looked at them and said, 'With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.'" - Matthew 19:26

source: Traditional Catholic Devotion to St. Rita of Cascia
notes: St. Rita is one of the most popular saints in the Catholic Church. Her incorrupt body is venerated in the Basilica of St. Rita in Cascia, Italy. She is the patron saint of impossible causes, desperate situations, difficult marriages, abuse victims, widows, mothers, and those who have lost loved ones. Her feast day is May 22, and many people pray her novena in preparation for her feast.
